brief.subject: FTC hits payment processor over hidden fees and auto-renewals
brief.headline: Payment Processor Pays $600,000 Over Hidden Fees; New Details in Amazon Ads Case
brief.dek: Regulators target undisclosed fees and auto-renewing contracts, while unredacted filings detail alleged price inflation in Amazon's ad auctions.
brief.lede: A payment processor and its leasing affiliate will pay $600,000 to settle claims they hid fees and auto-renewing contracts from small businesses.

sections.heading: Hidden Fees Cost Processor $600,000
bullets: $600,000 settlement: Riverside Payments, Cascade Equipment Leasing and their operators resolve FTC and Washington state allegations.
Regulators allege the firms promised small businesses savings on card processing but didn't disclose fees.
Auto-renewing contracts were also allegedly concealed, a trap that also catches consumers in service agreements.
Takeaway for anyone signing a contract: check fee schedules and cancellation terms before agreeing.

sections.heading: Amazon Ad Case Gets More Detail
bullets: 22 states and the FTC filed an updated complaint with previously redacted details against Amazon.
Regulators allege Amazon secretly manipulated its search ad auctions to inflate prices.
The filing claims auction results were adjusted to hit corporate financial targets.
These are allegations in an active case, not findings, so watch how the court responds.
